scope: Exploratory method-development study; protocol fixed before this execution, not a preregistered external study
revision: run_05: retain run_04 joint-estimate rule and common fallback/accounting; cancel identical reference/target polynomial factors analytically in ALL variants, retaining the correct nonzero zero-excess tail limit. Candidate list, bands, meshes and thresholds remain unchanged; all earlier pilots preserved.
comparison_contract: Identical observations, priors, tolerances, phase/floor gates, rate-aware full-tail envelopes, LP solver and mesh schedule; isolate the additional rate-located physical-pair screening. Fixed-fine scan is secondary.
go_criteria: Zero opposite decisive labels between proposed and either baseline
Every accepted prediction contains the generating response and meets its declared tolerance in the tested cases
Every physical-pair region has finite-rate admissible spectra and independently checked kernel increments
Report LP work against the progressive comparator, not only against fixed-fine scans
Do not assert speedup if witness screening adds no work reduction or loses resolved decisions
limitations: Same four historical deterministic synthetic generating spectra, not independent new material trials
No physical mass/rate cap; a supplied cap changes the class and is rejected by this implementation
Known polynomial loading histories, known target input, zero prehistory and deterministic response bands
Input uncertainty is a common multiplicative envelope with known timing, not additive or timing error
Different target delays mean different requested responses; no improvement is claimed for the original earlier target
Only a finite candidate list is searched; neither continuum earliest time nor monotone diameter is assumed
The waiting exponent locates a physical witness rate; exact kernels determine exclusions, not a fitted asymptotic constant
LP residual checks and envelope padding are floating-point checks, not directed-rounding certificates
Shared LP-result caching is used for reproducible comparisons; logical LP counts and variable counts are compared, not wall-clock speed
No new general LP solver, universally better point predictor or globally novel search principle is claimed
